NITA-U says the National Backbone Infrastructure became operational in 2013/14 and, across four completed phases, links Kampala to towns including Mbale, Gulu, Fort Portal and Mbarara, with 7 border points connected.
NITA-U says Phase III fibre created an alternative route to the undersea cables via Mutukula to Dar es Salaam, with 7 border points connected to the NBI.
facts.system: NBI Mutukula route to Dar es Salaam

facts.fact: NITA-U, the government's IT authority, completed and operates the National Backbone Infrastructure connecting 603 ministries, departments, agencies, local government sites and service centres.

NITA-U says 603 ministries, departments, agencies, local government sites and government service centres are connected to the government network, with the last-mile project having connected 575 of 700 sites; no count of local governments is given.
The Ministry of ICT secured funding for the NBI/EGI and NITA-U, a government authority, completed and runs it.

UGA.note: The USD 70 per Mbps is a government bandwidth price, not a mobile data price.
